source.title: A discussion about digital governance frameworks — AI and Society Seminar Series at University of Wellington
source.description: A [seminar](https://ecs.wgtn.ac.nz/Groups/AI_and_Society/AI_and_Society_Seminars) at Te Kura Mātai Pūkaha, Pūrorohiko (School of Engineering and Computer Science) of Wellington, organised by professor Ali Knott. Originally published on the [Wellington University website](https://vstream.au.panopto.com/Panopto/Pages/Viewer.aspx?id=c021fed5-7bd8-456b-aaab-b41300612e06&start=0) alongside notes. In this talk, Matti presents a digital governance initiative he's working on. OpenFisca is a Rules as Code system used around the world to model tax and benefit systems. The OpenFisca Association was established to govern the way OpenFisca as an open source project is maintained, used, funded and developed over time. This project has been recognised internationally, including as digital public infrastructure, digital public good, and digital common. We also discuss how digital governance frameworks could be applied to sovereign AI projects, and other digital infrastructure.

editorial.why_selected: A university seminar on digital governance frameworks for AI, from the team behind OpenFisca, the open-source rules-as-code engine.
learning_outcomes: How laws get translated into code, and what's lost
Governance frameworks for algorithmic public services
editorial.try_next: Look at OpenFisca's public rules for one benefit and compare them with the law's wording.
